integrity: The proof starts from the independently verified perfect-graph facet description, derives exact arbitrary-center distance constraints, uses a maximum clique for the global upper bound, and proves sharpness at the uniform center. The full center locus, uniqueness criterion, and tangent facets are derived from equality conditions. Finite checks are corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to nonempty finite perfect graphs and the canonical characteristic-vector realization with the standard Euclidean metric. It does not extend unchanged to nonperfect graphs, where additional stable-set facets may reduce the inradius. A residual originality risk remains for an equivalent folklore observation or a differently phrased general Chebyshev-center result.
title: Clique number controls the exact Euclidean inradius of every perfect stable-set polytope
